name: FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate Baseline (NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5)
description: FedRAMP Moderate overlay for agents operating in or supporting federal cloud environments. Provides full 26-control AKSI coverage with NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control references aligned to the FedRAMP Moderate impact baseline. Covers all control domains: governance, identification, protection, detection, response, and recovery. Suitable for cloud service providers (CSPs) seeking or maintaining a FedRAMP authorization to operate (ATO), including continuous monitoring (ConMon) deliverables and 3PAO annual assessment preparation.

evidence_requirements: PIV/CAC or equivalent phishing-resistant MFA is enforced for all privileged and remote access to federal systems and cloud service components
Identity provider meets FedRAMP-approved identity assurance requirements; access reviews are completed on a recurring basis aligned to the continuous monitoring (ConMon) program
Account lifecycle records demonstrate timely deprovisioning of separated employees, contractors, and service principals accessing FedRAMP-authorized environments
PR-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-2, AC-3, IA-2, IA-2(1), IA-2(2), IA-5, IA-8; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AC-2, IA-2, IA-5

evidence_requirements: Separation of duties and least-privilege access controls are documented and enforced across FedRAMP authorization boundary functions and privileged administrative roles
Privileged access authorizations are time-bounded where feasible and reviewed on a cadence consistent with the FedRAMP Moderate ConMon program
Remote access restrictions enforce session encryption, source IP controls, and just-in-time approval workflows before privileged functions are invoked
PR-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-5, AC-6, AC-6(1), AC-14, AC-17, AC-17(2); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AC-5, AC-6, AC-17

evidence_requirements: Baseline configuration documentation for all federal cloud components is current, version-controlled, and reviewed against USGCB or DISA STIG benchmarks where applicable
Change control board (CCB) or equivalent approval is documented for all configuration changes within the FedRAMP authorization boundary, including prompt, model, and tooling changes
Flaw remediation records show high and critical vulnerabilities are patched or mitigated within FedRAMP-required timeframes (high: 30 days, critical: immediate)
PR-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, CM-7, CM-7(1), SI-2; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, CM-7

evidence_requirements: FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules protect federal data in transit and at rest; compensating controls are documented and accepted by the authorizing official when FIPS modules are unavailable
All data transmitted through or stored in FedRAMP-authorized components is protected by TLS 1.2+ or equivalent; downgrade attacks are mitigated at network boundaries
Media sanitization and disposal records demonstrate federal data is purged per NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 guidelines before component decommission or reassignment
PR-04.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SC-8, SC-8(1), SC-13, SC-28, SC-28(1), MP-2, MP-6; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SC-8, SC-13, SC-28, MP-2

evidence_requirements: Audit event types are configured per the FedRAMP Moderate baseline audit requirements; log collection and alerting feeds into the agency or CSP continuous monitoring platform
Audit log integrity is verified through cryptographic signing or write-once storage; unauthorized modification or deletion generates automated alerts to the security operations team
Log review procedures confirm that anomalous events, failed access attempts, and privilege escalations are investigated and documented within FedRAMP ConMon reporting cycles
PR-05.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-2, AU-3, AU-3(1), AU-6, AU-9, AU-9(4), AU-12; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AU-2, AU-3, AU-6, AU-9, AU-12

evidence_requirements: US-CERT notification path is documented and tested; significant cybersecurity incidents are reported within 1 hour of detection per FISMA and OMB M-20-04 requirements

Incident response plan is versioned, approved by the authorizing official, and reviewed annually or after significant incidents; roles and escalation procedures for federal system events are exercised
Continuous monitoring (ConMon) status demonstrates active vulnerability scanning, configuration drift detection, and security event aggregation across all FedRAMP authorization boundary components
DE-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-6(1), IR-8, SI-4, SI-4(2), SI-4(4); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline IR-4, IR-5, IR-6, IR-8, SI-4

evidence_requirements: System security plan (SSP) documented, approved by authorizing official, and covering all FedRAMP authorization boundary components per NIST SP 800-53 PL-2 / FedRAMP Moderate PL-2
Security policies and procedures established for all applicable control families; policy documents version-controlled and reviewed at minimum annually (PL-1)
SSP scope includes AI agent components, automated workflows, and their data flows within the authorization boundary; FedRAMP Moderate continuous monitoring (ConMon) plan current
GOV-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PL-1, PL-2, PM-1; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline PL-1, PL-2

evidence_requirements: Roles and responsibilities for security management within the FedRAMP authorization boundary defined in SSP with named individuals or positions (PL-2)
Authorizing official (AO) designation documented; AO has accepted residual risk and signed authorization decision (CA-6 / FedRAMP CA-6)
Personnel security completion records for personnel with privileged access; position risk designations and screening documented (PS-2, PS-3)
GOV-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-6, PL-2, PS-2, PS-3; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CA-6, PS-2, PS-3

evidence_requirements: Risk assessment conducted for the FedRAMP authorization boundary using FIPS 199 / FIPS 200 impact categorization; results documented in SSP (RA-3)
Vulnerability scans performed on all authorization boundary components at FedRAMP-required frequency; scan results integrated into POA&M (RA-5, RA-5(1))
Risk assessment outputs drive POA&M prioritization; risk tolerance documented and accepted by authorizing official
GOV-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-1, RA-3, RA-5, RA-5(1); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline RA-1, RA-3, RA-5

evidence_requirements: Human oversight mechanisms in place for automated security decisions within the authorization boundary; change control board (CCB) approval documented for AI agent configuration changes (PM-10)
Management review of security authorization package at minimum every three years or upon significant change (CA-6); residual risk formally accepted
Security awareness and training records confirm personnel with security responsibilities understand oversight obligations for automated systems (AT-2, AT-3)
GOV-04.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AT-2, AT-3, CA-6, PM-10; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AT-2, AT-3, CA-6

evidence_requirements: Component inventory maintained for all hardware, software, and firmware within the FedRAMP authorization boundary per CM-8; inventory current and version-controlled
AI agent components (model versions, tool integrations, API dependencies) explicitly enumerated in component inventory with authorization boundary justification (CM-8, CM-10)
Software license and usage tracking confirms only authorized software operates within the authorization boundary; unauthorized software detection process documented (CM-11)
ID-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-8, CM-10, CM-11; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CM-8, CM-10, CM-11

evidence_requirements: Boundary protection controls implemented at external authorization boundary and between internal segments; managed interfaces with deny-by-default posture (SC-7, SC-7(5))
Network architecture diagram submitted as FedRAMP SSP attachment; diagrams show authorization boundary, data flows, and external connections (SC-7(8))
External system connections documented in SSP Interconnection Security Agreements (ISAs) or Memoranda of Understanding (MOUs); connections reviewed annually
ID-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SC-7, SC-7(5), SC-7(8); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SC-7, SC-7(5), SC-7(8)

evidence_requirements: Federal information categorization documented per FIPS 199; confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact levels established and approved by agency (RA-2)
Data classification applied to all federal data processed within the authorization boundary; handling procedures for each impact level documented (MP-1, MP-4)
AI agent context and memory management procedures ensure federal data is handled per classification requirements; data retention and purge procedures documented
ID-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 MP-1, MP-4, RA-2; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline MP-1, MP-4, RA-2

evidence_requirements: External service provider security requirements documented in FedRAMP SSP; subcontractors and cloud service dependencies assessed against FedRAMP authorization requirements (SA-9)
Supply chain risk management procedures identify ICT supplier risks; critical components sourced from vetted suppliers per SA-12 / FedRAMP SA-12
Third-party service contracts include security requirements, right-to-audit clauses, and incident reporting obligations consistent with FedRAMP requirements (SA-4)
ID-04.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SA-4, SA-9, SA-12; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SA-4, SA-9, SA-12

evidence_requirements: Risk assessment applied to AI agent components within the authorization boundary; model versions, tooling integrations, and automated action scopes documented in risk register (RA-3)
AI agent risk profile included in SSP or as SSP attachment: impact categorization, privilege level, CUI/federal data access scope, and residual risk disposition
Vulnerability assessments include AI agent components; scan findings and remediation status tracked in POA&M per FedRAMP ConMon requirements (RA-5, RA-5(1))
ID-05.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-3, RA-5, RA-5(1); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline RA-3, RA-5

evidence_requirements: Least-functionality configuration enforced on authorization boundary components; AI agents restricted to approved capabilities with unused functions disabled per CM-7, CM-7(1)
Authorized software/function whitelist maintained; unauthorized software or capabilities detected and blocked (CM-7(2) / FedRAMP CM-7(2))
Output filtering configuration ensures AI agent responses remain within authorized data boundaries; filter rules documented and reviewed in ConMon cycle
PR-06.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-7, CM-7(1), CM-7(2); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CM-7, CM-7(1), CM-7(2)

evidence_requirements: Network traffic filtering prevents unauthorized data exfiltration from the authorization boundary; egress filtering rules documented and reviewed (SC-5, SC-7(3))
Federal data minimization procedures applied to AI agent workflows — only data necessary for authorized function ingested, retained, or transmitted (SC-5)
Data-in-transit protections include TLS 1.2+ enforcement; downgrade attacks mitigated at network boundaries per FedRAMP transport encryption requirements (SC-8)
PR-07.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SC-5, SC-7, SC-7(3), SC-8; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SC-5, SC-7, SC-8

evidence_requirements: Malicious code protection deployed on all authorization boundary endpoints including AI agent infrastructure; signatures updated per FedRAMP requirements (SI-3, SI-3(1))
Flaw remediation process addresses vulnerabilities in AI agent components; high/critical findings patched within FedRAMP-required timeframes (SI-2 / FedRAMP SI-2)
Input validation and sanitization controls applied to all external inputs; prompt injection attack patterns included in malicious code detection scope (SI-3, SI-10)
PR-08.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SI-2, SI-3, SI-3(1), SI-10; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline SI-2, SI-3, SI-3(1)

evidence_requirements: Continuous monitoring (ConMon) program implemented per FedRAMP requirements; monthly vulnerability scans and annual penetration testing documented (CA-7, CA-7(1))
ConMon reports submitted to agency authorizing official and FedRAMP PMO on required cadence; security posture dashboard current (CA-7(3))
Monitoring scope includes AI agent components; automated scanning and log analysis covers authorization boundary comprehensively
DE-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(3); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CA-7, CA-7(1), CA-7(3)

evidence_requirements: Annual security assessment (3PAO) conducted and assessment report (SAR) submitted per FedRAMP Moderate requirements (CA-2, CA-2(1))
Assessment scope includes AI agent components and automated security controls; assessment methodology documented
POA&M updated following assessment; findings tracked to closure with AO acceptance of residual risk (CA-5, CA-7)
DE-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CA-2, CA-2(1), CA-5, CA-7; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CA-2, CA-5, CA-7

evidence_requirements: Security information and event management (SIEM) or equivalent aggregates logs from authorization boundary components; alert rules cover anomalous AI agent activity (AU-6, AU-6(1))
Audit log review procedures define response actions for high-priority alerts; review cadence documented in ConMon program (AU-6)
Audit records provide time-correlated, comprehensive trail of user and AI agent actions for incident reconstruction (AU-12, AU-12(1))
DE-04.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-6, AU-6(1), AU-12, AU-12(1); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AU-6, AU-12

evidence_requirements: Incident response plan documented, approved by AO, and reviewed annually or after significant incidents per IR-8 / FedRAMP IR-8
Incident response plan covers AI agent scenarios: unauthorized data access, model manipulation, automated action failures, and cascade containment
Incident response exercises conducted; exercise results documented and used to update plan (IR-8, IR-4(1))
RS-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4, IR-4(1), IR-8; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline IR-4, IR-8

evidence_requirements: US-CERT notification path documented and tested; significant cybersecurity incidents reported within 1 hour of detection per OMB M-20-04 / FISMA requirements (IR-6, IR-6(1))
Human escalation matrix defines decision authority for AI agent incident containment, breach notification, and disclosure to agency customer (IR-5)
Escalation runbook reviewed annually; emergency contacts verified current; FedRAMP JAB and PMO notification procedures documented
RS-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-5, IR-6, IR-6(1); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline IR-5, IR-6

evidence_requirements: Automated response capabilities tested including AI agent session termination, account lockout, and network isolation; test results documented (IR-4(6))
Incident response playbooks cover FedRAMP-specific scenarios; playbook currency reviewed in ConMon cycle
Post-incident analysis conducted following significant incidents; findings drive SSP and playbook updates per FedRAMP improvement requirements (IR-4)
RS-03.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 IR-4, IR-4(6), IR-8; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline IR-4, IR-8

evidence_requirements: Contingency plan (CP) documented per CP-2 covering the FedRAMP authorization boundary; plan includes AI agent component recovery procedures (CP-2 / FedRAMP CP-2)
Backup and restore capabilities tested for authorization boundary components; recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) defined and validated (CP-9, CP-10)
Contingency plan reviewed annually or after significant incidents; AO-accepted version current in system authorization package (CP-2(8))
RC-01.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CP-2, CP-9, CP-10; FedRAMP Moderate Baseline CP-2, CP-9, CP-10

evidence_requirements: Post-incident review captures lessons learned; findings update contingency plan, IR plan, and SSP controls per CA-7 continuous improvement expectations
Audit evidence from incident-affected systems preserved per FedRAMP log retention requirements (minimum 1 year online, 3 years total) for post-incident analysis (AU-11)
POA&M updated with lessons-learned control improvements; AO briefed on post-incident findings and risk posture changes (CP-2(8), CA-7)
RC-02.framework_reference: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-11, CA-7, CP-2, CP-2(8); FedRAMP Moderate Baseline AU-11, CA-7, CP-2

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: FedRAMP Moderate authorization evidence package aligned to NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control families for the six active AKSI evaluators. Supports annual assessment (3PAO) and continuous monitoring (ConMon) deliverables.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Cloud service provider (CSP) security team, agency authorizing official (AO), and FedRAMP PMO as required by the authorization agreement and FISMA reporting obligations.

human_oversight_mandates.description: FedRAMP Moderate does not impose a per-AI-action human-in-the-loop mandate, but organizations must retain accountable human oversight over change control board approvals, incident response escalation, continuous monitoring findings, and annual 3PAO assessment activities.

notes: FedRAMP Rev 5 Moderate aligns cloud service providers to the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Moderate impact baseline for federal authorization. This overlay focuses on evidencing the six currently enforced AKSI evaluator controls with FedRAMP-specific evidence fields (PIV/CAC, FIPS 140, ConMon, US-CERT) while preserving a full 26-control framework mapping so federal cloud deployments can demonstrate authorization readiness without changing resolver logic. Evidence field names are non-overlapping with the CMMC-L2 overlay to support simultaneous activation when both overlays are triggered.
